# Leachate flow and monitoring network for Zelena Petlja’s temporary storage yard

## Verified facts
- The Subotica Environmental Inspectorate ordered four groundwater monitoring wells installed and a remediation proposal submitted within 120 days, with the deadline in late June 2024. [F1]
- Only a 1993 hydrogeological sketch exists, and the company does not know the contamination extent or seasonal groundwater-flow direction. [F2]
- The company needs a leachate containment and treatment proposal acceptable to the inspectorate, not only a monitoring exercise. [F3]
- The yard liner was never designed for liquid retention, and the company’s own COD sample was 3,400 mg/L, well above the threshold that triggers a formal response. [F4]
- The company reports no dedicated research budget or laboratory beyond the basic wet-chemistry bench used for leachate monitoring. [F5]
- The researcher’s industry experience includes advising on site characterisation methodology and monitoring network design. [F6]
- His field work includes a dense multi-level piezometer network and particle-tracking transport simulation at a production well field. [F7]
- He is open to joint projects with companies in environmental monitoring and to contract research on site-specific hydrogeological assessment. [F8]

## Our inference
- The documented field sites are bank-filtration, agricultural-recharge and canal settings, not waste-yard leachate; this suggests the monitoring and modelling methods are likely transferable in principle but must be tested here before being relied on for the inspectorate proposal.
- The researcher’s availability in spring 2024 is recorded as unknown, so the schedule and this joint project are conditional on early confirmation.
- The 3,400 mg/L COD comes from the company’s bench, so the inspectorate may require accredited confirmation; the first sampling should pair bench measurements with an external laboratory check.

## Proposed next steps
- First experiment (weeks 1–6): use the 1993 sketch, yard records and the company’s 3,400 mg/L COD result as baseline. Before final well siting, the researcher proposes a short transect of four temporary shallow piezometers across the eastern fence line; the company provides yard history, liner details and bench COD/heavy-metal data. Measure hydraulic head, depth to water, COD and specific conductance at each point, then repeat once after a rainfall/recharge event, changing one suspected factor—groundwater level—while holding locations fixed. Go/no-go: proceed to final four-well design and containment options only if a consistent hydraulic gradient and COD decrease away from the yard are observed; if gradients contradict the sketch or the plume misses the transect, re-site before drilling; if boundary COD stays above the trigger threshold, containment must be in the proposal. Success would be a defensible flow-direction estimate from two rounds.
- Proposed timeline: weeks 1–2 data review and regulator requirements; weeks 3–6 reconnaissance; weeks 7–12 final four-well installation and two sampling rounds; weeks 13–17 draft containment/treatment proposal. Proposed success criteria: a flow-direction estimate, a COD plume bounded at the yard boundary with at least one downgradient well, and an inspectorate-ready proposal.
- After the first field results, the researcher would draft containment and treatment options; the company would supply cost and site-operation constraints. This is a proposal for negotiation, not an agreed design or budget.
- Before drilling, agree in writing who funds drilling, permits and accredited laboratory analyses; the company’s material shows no dedicated research budget, so external funding or cost-sharing is a precondition, not a commitment.

## Open questions
- Can the researcher confirm availability to start field work within the 120-day window in spring 2024, since availability is recorded as unknown?
- Who will carry out and fund drilling and installation of the four wells, and which permits are required?
- What site information exists beyond the 1993 sketch: depth to water table, liner details, existing boreholes, and nearby production or monitoring wells?
- Which parameters and analytical standards will the Subotica Environmental Inspectorate require, and is an accredited laboratory available for confirmatory analyses?
- What waste types and volumes were stored in the yard over twelve years, and were hazardous items present that could change leachate composition?
